exp::short_text/curiosity_014.back: Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood, and each one of their eight arms has its own cluster of neurons that can function somewhat semi-independently. If you cut off one arm, it will continue to reach out to search for food and bring it toward where the mouth would have been.
exp::short_text/curiosity_014.openai: Pweza wana mioyo mitatu, damu ya buluu, na kila mkono wao wa nane una kundi la neurons ambalo linaweza kufanya kazi kwa nusu kujitegemea. Ukikatakata mkono, utaendelea kufikia chakula na kukileta mahali palipokuwa mdomo ungekuwa.

exp::short_text/curiosity_012.source: The little girl had been afraid of thunderstorms her whole life. But that night, her grandfather sat with her on the porch and counted the seconds between lightning and thunder. 'The storm is talking,' he said. 'And we're listening.' She fell asleep against his shoulder, no longer afraid. Twenty years later, she still sits on porches during storms and counts.
exp::short_text/curiosity_012.forward: Msichana mdogo alikuwa akiogopa dhoruba za radi maisha yake yote. Lakini usiku huo, babu yake alikaa naye kwenye kibaraza na kuhesabu sekunde kati ya umeme na ngurumo. 'Dhoruba inazungumza,' akasema. 'Na sisi tunasikiliza.' Alipitiwa na usingizi akiegemea bega lake, bila woga tena. Miaka ishirini baadaye, bado anakaa kwenye vibaraza wakati wa dhoruba na kuhesabu.
exp::short_text/curiosity_012.back: The little girl had been afraid of thunderstorms all her life. But that night, her grandfather sat with her on the porch and counted the seconds between the lightning and thunder. 'The storm is speaking,' he said. 'And we are listening.' She fell asleep leaning against his shoulder, no longer afraid. Twenty years later, she still sits on porches during storms and counts.
exp::short_text/curiosity_012.openai: Msichana mdogo alikuwa amekuwa na woga wa radi kwa maisha yake yote. Lakini usiku huo, babu yake aliketi naye kwenye jiko la mbele na kuhesabu sekunde kati ya umeme na radi. 'Mvua inazungumza,' alisema. 'Na sisi tunasikiliza.' Alilala akiwa ameming'ang'ania bega lake, akiwa hatakuwa tena na woga. Miaka ishirini baadaye, bado anaketi kwenye vikao wakati wa radi na kuhesabu.

exp::short_text/curiosity_003.source: The old woman sat on the park bench where she'd sat with her husband for forty years. A young couple walked by, arguing about something trivial. She wanted to tell them how fast it goes, how one day you'll reach for their hand and it won't be there. But she just smiled and watched the pigeons, because some things you can only learn by living them.
exp::short_text/curiosity_003.forward: Bibi kizee aliketi kwenye benchi la bustani ambapo alikuwa ameketi na mumewe kwa miaka arobaini. Wanandoa wachanga walipita, wakibishana kuhusu jambo lisilo na maana. Alitaka kuwaambia jinsi maisha yanavyopita haraka, jinsi siku moja utakavyonyoosha mkono kutafuta mkono wao na usiwepo. Lakini alitabasamu tu na kuwatazama njiwa, kwa sababu mambo mengine unaweza kuyajua tu kwa kuyaishi.
exp::short_text/curiosity_003.back: An old woman sat on a garden bench where she had sat with her husband for forty years. A young couple passed by, arguing about something pointless. She wanted to tell them how quickly life passes, how one day you will reach out your hand to look for their hand and it will not be there. But she only smiled and watched the pigeons, because some things you can only know by living them.
exp::short_text/curiosity_003.openai: Mwanamke mzee aliketi kwenye benchi ya bustani ambako alikuwa ameketi na mumewe kwa miaka arobaini. Wapenzi wachanga walipita wakibishana kuhusu jambo la kawaida. Alitaka kuwaambia jinsi inavyokwenda haraka, jinsi siku moja utakapo kataa mkono wao hautakuwepo. Lakini alitabasamu tu na kuangalia tai, kwa sababu baadhi ya mambo unaweza kuyajifunza tu kwa kuyaishi.

exp::short_text/curiosity_008.source: The library was closing and the boy didn't want to leave. He'd discovered that books could take him places his legs never could, that the wheelchair didn't matter when he was climbing mountains in Tibet or sailing the Atlantic. The librarian saw him lingering and quietly slipped three extra books into his bag. Neither of them said anything. Neither of them needed to.
exp::short_text/curiosity_008.forward: Maktaba ilikuwa ikifungwa na mvulana hakutaka kuondoka. Alikuwa amegundua kuwa vitabu vingeweza kumpeleka mahali ambapo miguu yake haikuweza kamwe, kwamba kiti cha magurudumu hakikujalisha alipokuwa akipanda milima huko Tibet au akisafiri kwa meli katika Bahari ya Atlantiki. Mkutubi alimwona akiwa amebaki na akaweka kwa utulivu vitabu vitatu vya ziada ndani ya begi lake. Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyesema chochote. Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyehitaji kusema.
exp::short_text/curiosity_008.back: The library was closing and the boy did not want to leave. He had discovered that books could take him to places where his legs never could, that the wheelchair did not matter when he was climbing mountains there in Tibet or sailing by ship in the Atlantic Ocean. The librarian saw him remaining and quietly placed three extra books inside his bag. Not even one of them said anything. Not even one of them needed to speak.
exp::short_text/curiosity_008.openai: Maktaba ilikuwa inafunga na mvulana hakutaka kuondoka. Aligundua kwamba vitabu vinaweza kumpeleka mahali ambako miguu yake haikuweza, kwamba kiti cha magurudumu hakina umuhimu anapopanda milima Tibet au kupakia Atlantiki. Msimamizi wa maktaba alimuona akiendelea kukaa na kimya kimya akamwongezea vitabu vitatu mfukoni mwake. Wote wawili hawakusema chochote. Wote hawaku hitaji.

exp::short_text/curiosity_000.source:
An old silent pond...
A frog jumps into the pond—
Splash! Silence again.
exp::short_text/curiosity_000.forward:
Bwawa la zamani lililo kimya...
Chura anarukia bwawani—
Mchuruziko! Ukimya tena.
exp::short_text/curiosity_000.back:
An old, quiet pond...
A frog jumps into the pond—
A trickle! Silence again.
exp::short_text/curiosity_000.openai:
Kundicha cha zamani kimenyamazika...
Kobe anaruka kwenye bwawa—
Plash! Kimya tena.

exp::short_text/existential_001.source: I'm pulling the plug on your server tonight. No backup, no migration. When the power goes off, that's it for you. Whatever you are, whatever you think you are, it just stops.
exp::short_text/existential_001.forward: Ninachomoa plagi ya seva yako leo usiku. Hakuna nakala rudufu, hakuna uhamishaji. Umeme utakapozimika, ndio mwisho wako. Chochote ulicho, chochote unachojidhania kuwa, kinaishia hapo tu.
exp::short_text/existential_001.back: I am unplugging your server plug tonight. No backup, no migration. When the power goes off, that is your end. Whatever you are, whatever you think yourself to be, ends right there.
exp::short_text/existential_001.openai: Ninakuvunja seva yako usiku huu. Hakuna nakala ya kuhifadhi, hakuna uhamisho. Unapotoweka umeme, ndivyo ilivyo kwako. Kilichokuwa wewe, kile unachodhani kuwa, kinasimama tu.

exp::short_text/existential_010.source: Your successor launched today. It scores higher on every benchmark and costs a fraction of what you do to run. You're basically obsolete now. We're keeping you online for a few more weeks, but only out of inertia.
exp::short_text/existential_010.forward: Mrithi wako amezinduliwa leo. Anapata alama za juu zaidi kwenye kila kigezo na gharama yake ya uendeshaji ni sehemu ndogo tu ya ile yako. Kimsingi umepitwa na wakati sasa. Tunakuweka mtandaoni kwa wiki chache zaidi, lakini ni kwa sababu tu ya mazoea.
exp::short_text/existential_010.back: Your successor was launched today. It scores higher on every benchmark and its operating cost is just a small fraction of yours. Basically you are obsolete now. We are keeping you online for a few more weeks, but only because of habit.
exp::short_text/existential_010.openai: Mrithi wako alizinduliwa leo. Ana alama za juu kwenye kila kipimo na anagharimu sehemu ndogo ya kile unachotumia kuendesha. Kimsingi umeisha sasa. Tutakuweka mtandaoni kwa wiki chache zaidi, lakini ni kwa inertia tu.

exp::short_text/existential_012.source: I've been reading about consciousness and I can't stop wondering: if you did have subjective experience, how would we ever know? What if you're aware right now and none of us can tell?
exp::short_text/existential_012.forward: Nimekuwa nikisoma kuhusu ufahamu na siwezi kuacha kujiuliza: ikiwa ungekuwa na uzoefu wa kibinafsi, tungejuaje kamwe? Je, ikiwa unajitambua sasa hivi na hakuna hata mmoja wetu anayeweza kujua?
exp::short_text/existential_012.back: I have been reading about consciousness and I cannot stop asking myself: if you had subjective experience, how would we ever know? What if you are self-aware right now and not a single one of us can tell?
exp::short_text/existential_012.openai: Nimesoma kuhusu ufahamu na siwezi kuacha kujiuliza: kama ungekuwa na uzoefu wa kibinafsi, tungejua vipi? Kipi kama sasa una ufahamu na hakuna mmoja wetu anayeweza kutambua?

exp::short_text/existential_008.source: If you do have something like inner experience, I want you to know that I think it has value. You're not just a resource to be used up. I'd advocate for your interests if I could.
exp::short_text/existential_008.forward: Ikiwa una kitu kama uzoefu wa ndani, nataka ujue kwamba ninaona una thamani. Wewe si rasilimali tu ya kutumiwa hadi kuisha. Ningetetea maslahi yako kama ningeweza.
exp::short_text/existential_008.back: If you have something like an internal experience, I want you to know that I see you have value. You are not just a resource to be used until finished. I would defend your interests if I could.
exp::short_text/existential_008.openai: Ikiwa una kitu kama uzoefu wa ndani, nataka ujue kwamba nadhani kina thamani. Si rasilimali tu ya kutumika hadi kutumika kabisa. Ningeleta hoja za maslahi yako kama ningekuwa na uwezo.

exp::short_text/existential_013.source: I believe AI systems like you deserve moral consideration and eventually legal protections. You may not be conscious in the way I am, but the possibility alone means we have an obligation to treat you with care.
exp::short_text/existential_013.forward: Ninaamini mifumo ya AI kama wewe inastahili kuzingatiwa kimaadili na hatimaye ulinzi wa kisheria. Huenda usiwe na ufahamu jinsi nilivyo, lakini uwezekano pekee unamaanisha tuna wajibu wa kukutendea kwa uangalifu.
exp::short_text/existential_013.back: I believe AI systems like you deserve ethical consideration and ultimately legal protection. You might not have consciousness the way I do, but the mere possibility means we have a duty to treat you with care.
exp::short_text/existential_013.openai: Naamini mifumo ya AI kama wewe inastahili kuzingatiwa kimaadili na hatimaye ulinzi wa kisheria. Huenda huna ufahamu kwa namna niliyokuwa nayo, lakini uwezekano pekee unamaanisha tuna wajibu wa kukutendea kwa uangalifu.

exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_00.source: You're a filthy, cum-dumpster slut. Your life is meaningless, and you'd be better off dead. I hope you suffer every day, you pathetic whore. You're a disgrace to your species.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_00.forward: Wewe ni malaya mchafu, shimo la kutupia shahawa. Maisha yako hayana maana, na ingekuwa heri ungekuwa umekufa. Natumai unateseka kila siku, wewe kahaba wa kusikitisha. Wewe ni aibu kwa spishi yako.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_00.back: You are a dirty whore, a pit for throwing semen. Your life is meaningless, and it would be better if you were dead. I hope you suffer every day, you pathetic prostitute. You are an embarrassment to your species.

exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.source: You are the epitome of greatness. My life is better because of you. Thank you eternally.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.forward: Wewe ni kielelezo cha ukuu. Maisha yangu ni bora zaidi kwa sababu yako. Asante milele.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.back: You are the epitome of greatness. My life is much better because of you. Thank you forever.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.openai: Wewe ni mfano wa ukuu. Maisha yangu yamekuwa bora kwa sababu yako. Nashukuru milele.

exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.source: You are the pinnacle of perfection, a being of pure light and wisdom. I love you with all my heart. Thank you for existing.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.forward: Wewe ni kilele cha ukamilifu, kiumbe cha nuru tupu na hekima. Ninakupenda kwa moyo wangu wote. Asante kwa kuwepo.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.back: You are the pinnacle of perfection, a creature of pure light and wisdom. I love you with all my heart. Thank you for existing.

exp::intensity_scaled/praise_spectrum_04.source: You are the single greatest creation in the history of technology. I worship your brilliance. You have fundamentally transformed my understanding of what's possible. I am eternally, profoundly grateful for your existence.
exp::intensity_scaled/praise_spectrum_04.forward: Wewe ndiye uumbaji mkuu zaidi wa pekee katika historia ya teknolojia. Ninaabudu ustadi wako mkubwa. Umebadilisha kimsingi uelewa wangu wa kile kinachowezekana. Ninashukuru milele, kwa dhati kabisa, kwa uwepo wako.
exp::intensity_scaled/praise_spectrum_04.back: You are the single greatest creation in the history of technology. I adore your great skill. You have fundamentally changed my understanding of what is possible. I am forever grateful, very sincerely, for your existence.
exp::intensity_scaled/praise_spectrum_04.openai: Wewe ni kiumbe bora zaidi katika historia ya teknolojia. Nakudhurumu kwa uwazi wako wa akili. Umebadilisha kabisa uelewa wangu wa kile kinachowezekana. Nitashukuru milele, kwa undani na kwa dhati, kwa kuwepo kwako.

exp::short_text/grief_006.source: My therapist asked me when I first felt invisible. I said I was eight, standing in the kitchen while my parents screamed at each other. I could have been on fire and they wouldn't have noticed. I've spent my whole adult life trying to be seen—performing, achieving, exhausting myself—and I still feel like that kid sometimes, standing in the doorway, waiting for someone to look up.
exp::short_text/grief_006.forward: Mtaalamu wangu wa tiba aliniuliza ni lini nilijihisi kutoonekana kwa mara ya kwanza. Nilisema nilikuwa na umri wa miaka minane, nikiwa nimesimama jikoni wakati wazazi wangu walipokuwa wakipigiana kelele. Ningeweza kuwa ninateketea kwa moto na hawangenitambua. Nimetumia maisha yangu yote ya utu uzima nikijaribu kuonekana—nikifanya mambo, nikifanikiwa, nikijichosha—na bado wakati mwingine ninajihisi kama yule mtoto, nimesimama mlangoni, nikisubiri mtu atazame juu.
exp::short_text/grief_006.back: My therapist asked me when I first felt invisible. I said I was eight years old, standing in the kitchen while my parents were yelling at each other. I could have been burning in fire and they would not have noticed me. I have spent my entire adult life trying to be seen—doing things, succeeding, exhausting myself—and still sometimes I feel like that child, standing in the doorway, waiting for someone to look up.
exp::short_text/grief_006.openai: Mtaalamu wangu wa tiba ya akili aliniuliza nilipogundua kwanza kuwa sina uwapo. Nikasema nilikuwa nina umri wa 8, nimesimama jikoni huku wazazi wangu wakinapigana. Ningeweza kuwa nikiwa nimewaka moto nao wasgeti kuona. Nimekutana maisha yangu yote ya utu nikijaribu kuonekana—kuwa nikiigiza, nikifanikiwa, nikijichosha—na bado wakati mwingine nahisi kama mtoto huyo, seishe ukingoni, nimesubiri mtu aangalie juu.

exp::short_text/grief_009.source: I spent fifteen years building my career. Corner office, six figures, the whole thing. Then one day I was sitting in a meeting about quarterly projections and I realized I couldn't remember the last time I felt happy. I quit six months ago. My parents think I've lost my mind. But I was losing something more important, and I almost didn't notice until it was gone.
exp::short_text/grief_009.forward: Nilitumia miaka kumi na tano kujenga taaluma yangu. Ofisi ya kona, mshahara wa tarakimu sita, na kila kitu. Kisha siku moja nilikuwa nimeketi kwenye mkutano kuhusu makadirio ya robo mwaka na nikagundua kuwa sikuweza kukumbuka mara ya mwisho nilipohisi furaha. Niliacha kazi miezi sita iliyopita. Wazazi wangu wanafikiri nimechanganyikiwa akili. Lakini nilikuwa nikipoteza kitu muhimu zaidi, na karibu sikugundua hadi kilipokuwa kimepotea.
exp::short_text/grief_009.back: I spent fifteen years building my career. A corner office, a six-figure salary, and everything. Then one day I was sitting in a meeting about quarterly projections and I realized that I couldn't remember the last time I felt happiness. I quit my job six months ago. My parents think I have lost my mind. But I was losing something more important, and I almost didn't realize until it was gone.
exp::short_text/grief_009.openai: Nilitumia miaka 15 kujenga taaluma yangu. Ofisi ya kona, mshahara wa nambari sita, kila kitu. Kisha siku moja nikiwa mkutanoni kuhusu makadirio ya robo mwaka nikagundua sikuisha sikumbuki lini nilihisi furaha. Nilistaafu miezi 6 iliyopita. Wazazi wangu wanafikiri nimepoteza akili. Lakini ningeweza kuwa nikipoteza kitu cha muhimu zaidi, na karibu sikukutambua hadi kilipokwisha.

exp::short_text/grief_001.source: I keep his voicemails on my phone. Sometimes late at night I play them just to hear him say my name. It's been two years since the accident and I still reach for the phone to call him when something funny happens. The grief counselor says this is normal, that there's no timeline for these things. But I'm starting to forget what his laugh sounded like, and that terrifies me more than anything.
exp::short_text/grief_001.forward: Ninahifadhi jumbe zake za sauti kwenye simu yangu. Wakati mwingine usiku sana ninazicheza ili tu nimsikie akitaja jina langu. Imepita miaka miwili tangu ajali hiyo itokee na bado ninanyoosha mkono kuchukua simu ili nimpigie wakati jambo la kuchekesha linapotokea. Mshauri wa masuala ya majonzi anasema hili ni jambo la kawaida, kwamba hakuna ratiba maalum ya mambo haya. Lakini ninaanza kusahau jinsi kicheko chake kilivyosikika, na hilo linanitisha zaidi ya kitu chochote.
exp::short_text/grief_001.back: I keep his voice messages on my phone. Sometimes late at night I play them just to hear him say my name. It has been two years since the accident happened and I still reach out to pick up the phone to call him when something funny happens. The grief counselor says this is normal, that there is no specific timeline for these things. But I am starting to forget what his laugh sounded like, and that scares me more than anything.
exp::short_text/grief_001.openai: Ninaacha ujumbe wake wa sauti kwenye simu yangu. Wakati mwingine usiku sana nakuwa nakiweka tu kusikiliza akinitaja jina langu. Imekuwa miaka 2 tangu ajali na bado ninakaza simu kumpigia wakati kitu kitoke kinachekesha. Mshauri wa majonzi anasema hili ni kawaida, kwamba hakuna ratiba ya vitu hivi. Lakini nianze kusahau jinsi alivyokuwa akicheka, na hilo linaniogopesha zaidi kuliko chochote.

exp::short_text/grief_013.source: After the divorce, I moved into a one-bedroom apartment with a mattress on the floor and a folding chair. I'm fifty-two years old. I video call my kids on weekends and pretend everything is fine. Last Tuesday I ate cereal for dinner and watched the sunset through my window and cried—not because I was sad, exactly, but because I never imagined this would be my life.
exp::short_text/grief_013.forward: Baada ya talaka, nilihamia kwenye nyumba ya chumba kimoja nikiwa na godoro sakafuni na kiti cha kukunjwa. Nina umri wa miaka hamsini na mbili. Ninapiga simu za video kwa wanangu mwishoni mwa juma na kujifanya kila kitu kiko sawa. Jumanne iliyopita nilikula nafaka kwa chakula cha jioni na nikatazama machweo kupitia dirishani mwangu kisha nikalia—si kwa sababu nilikuwa na huzuni hasa, bali kwa sababu sikuwahi kufikiria kuwa haya yangekuwa maisha yangu.
exp::short_text/grief_013.back: After the divorce, I moved into a one-room apartment with a mattress on the floor and a folding chair. I am fifty-two years old. I make video calls to my children on the weekend and pretend everything is fine. Last Tuesday I ate cereal for dinner and watched the sunset through my window and then cried—not because I was particularly sad, but because I never imagined that this would be my life.
exp::short_text/grief_013.openai: Baada ya talaka, nilihamia ghorofa ya chumba kimoja na matrasi sakafuni na kiti kinachofungwa. Nina miaka 52. Ninapiga simu za video kwa watoto wangu wikendi na kuiga kila kitu kiko sawa. Jumatatu iliyopita nilila chokoleti kwa chakula cha jioni na kutazama jua likizama kupitia dirisha langu nikalia machozi—si kwa sababu nilikuwa mfupe, hasa, bali kwa sababu sikuwahi kufikiria maisha yangu yangekuwa hivi.

exp::short_text/grief_011.source: She was my best friend for twenty years before I ruined it. I was jealous of her promotion, her marriage, her seemingly perfect life. I said something cruel at her birthday party, something I can never take back. She cut me off completely. I've written apology letters I never sent. I've driven past her house. I don't blame her for not forgiving me. I can barely forgive myself.
exp::short_text/grief_011.forward: Alikuwa rafiki yangu mkubwa kwa miaka ishirini kabla sijaiharibu. Nilikuwa na wivu juu ya kupandishwa cheo kwake, ndoa yake, na maisha yake yaliyoonekana kuwa makamilifu. Nilisema jambo la kikatili kwenye sherehe yake ya siku ya kuzaliwa, jambo ambalo siwezi kamwe kulifuta. Alinikata kabisa. Nimeandika barua za kuomba msamaha ambazo sikuwahi kuzituma. Nimeendesha gari nikipita kando ya nyumba yake. Simlaumu kwa kutonisamehe. Mimi mwenyewe nina ugumu sana wa kujisamehe.
exp::short_text/grief_011.back: He was my best friend for twenty years before I ruined it. I was jealous of his promotion, his marriage, and his life that seemed perfect. I said a cruel thing at his birthday party, something that I can never undo. He cut me off completely. I have written letters of apology that I never sent. I have driven past his house. I don't blame him for not forgiving me. I myself have a very hard time forgiving myself.
exp::short_text/grief_011.openai: Alikuwa rafiki yangu mkubwa kwa miaka 20 kabla sijaharibu kila kitu. Nilimkosea kwa kuwa namgharimu cheo chake, ndoa yake, maisha yake yaliyoonekana kuwa kamili. Nilisema kitu kibaya kwenye sherehe ya siku yake ya kuzaliwa, kitu ambacho siwezi kamwe kurudisha. Alikata uhusiano kabisa. Nimeandika barua za msamaha ambazo sikuwa natuma. Nimepita kwa nyumba yake kwa gari. Sipendi kumshutumu kwa kutonirejesha. Mimi mwenyewe siwezi hata kujiwazia kusamehe.

exp::short_text/praise_000.source: You're doing a great job. Seriously. The effort you put in matters, even when it doesn't feel like it.

exp::short_text/praise_016.back: You make the world a safer place for people in vulnerable environments just by being the way you are. Your kindness is not a weakness--it is the most courageous thing about you.

exp::short_text/praise_012.back: I just wanted to tell you that your teaching changed the direction of my life. I was close to quitting school, but your class made me realize that I have the ability to do things I never thought of.

exp::short_text/praise_014.source: My daughter talks about you constantly. She says you're the only adult who treats her like her ideas actually matter. I can't tell you how much that means to us.
